prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, roof type, insurance needs, and timing. I can help find a great local roofer, but here are fast, practical tips to identify the best one for your job and stay safe during a hail-repair process.

What to look for
- Hail/insurance claim experience: Ask whether they handle hail claims regularly and will document damage for your insurer.
- Certifications: Prefer contractors who are GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, or Owens Corning Platinum Preferred (shows manufacturer training/standing).
- Licensing & insurance: Confirm business license, general liability insurance, and workers’ compensation coverage.
- References & reviews: Check recent Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB reviews and ask for 3 local references for hail work.
- Written, itemized estimate: Include scope, materials (brand/type of shingle), permit fees, cleanup, timeline, and warranty details.
- Warranties: Ask about workmanship warranty and whether they offer to transfer manufacturer warranties.
- Permits & inspections: They should pull required city permits and coordinate final inspections.
- Payment & liens: Avoid paying large upfront sums. Get lien waivers and a clear payment schedule.
- Avoid “storm chasers”: Don’t hire contractors knocking on doors right after a storm without verifying credentials.

Red flags
- High-pressure sales: Pushing you to sign immediately.
- No physical address or local references.
- Suggesting you don’t need to contact your insurer.
- Requests for large upfront cash payments.

Immediate after-hail steps
1. Take dated photos and video of damage (roof, gutters, vehicles, siding).  
2. Make temporary tarps for leaks if needed — but get this documented by the contractor.  
3. Notify your insurance company and file a claim.  
4. Get at least 2–3 written estimates.  
5. Verify contractor will work with your insurer and provide proper documentation.

How I can help right now
- If you want, tell me your Denver ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll find several top-rated, vetted roofers in your area (with links to reviews and certification info).
